page: Microsoft Azure F48as_v7 is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the Fasv7 family, powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V45 processor. This configuration features 48 physical cores and 48 vCPUs, operating at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz with a thread-per-core ratio of 1.0. The system is equipped with 192.0 GB of RAM, providing 4.0 GB of memory per core. Cache specifications include 48 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. The server does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable and runs on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Benchmark results place this server in the top tier (top 10%) for both single-core and multi-core CPU performance, with stress-ng scores of 3793.98 and 176853.77 respectively. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, reaching a top-tier read speed of 9266.23 GB/sec for small cached blocks and a strong 323.5 GB/sec for large uncached blocks. Cryptographic and compression capabilities are also notable, with single-threaded gzip compression at 41.1 GB/sec and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 674.49 GB/sec. Database operations perform in the top tier, as demonstrated by a PassMark database score of 39047.97 and Redis SET operations reaching 130.33 million operations per second.

For machine learning workloads, the server achieves top-tier performance in small-model LLM inference, processing 5215.56 tokens per second for prompts on a 135M model. However, performance drops to average levels (middle 50%) when processing larger 70B models, yielding 19.79 tokens per second for prompt processing and 4.1 tokens per second for text generation. This highlights a performance tradeoff for larger model architectures due to the lack of dedicated GPU hardware. This server is suited for CPU-intensive tasks, database operations, web serving, and small-scale language model inference.
